messages:
ana: kicking off staged cutover to v3 in eu-west1, shifting 20% to the new variant. noise in the first 10% — pods started but many went NotReady. anyone else seeing GPU allocation errors?
liam: saw some allocation failures flagged by node-exporter earlier. can you paste the pod events/logs? :thinking:
maria: cloud console shows we hit our regional T4 quota around 08:10 UTC — batch jobs ate most of it.
ana: pod events excerpt: 
```
Warning  FailedScheduling  2m (x5 over 6m)  default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 4 Insufficient gpu, 6 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
Warning  FailedCreatePodSandbox  1m  kubelet  Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to allocate gpu device
```
ops-sre: confirmed — T4 quota for eu-west1 is at 100%. Requesting a quota bump but cloud has a provisioning rate limit so it won't be instant.
deploy-bot: Canary-controller: status=paused (rolling failure > threshold) — automatic traffic rollback to 5% applied.
liam: the worse part: we manually adjusted a running pod's GPU request to 0.5 to test, but our GitOps operator keeps reconciling the repo and reverts it back to 2 GPUs. reconciler flips cause pod churn.
maria: here was the local Helm diff we applied (attempt):
```
resources:
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 1
  requests:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 0.5
```
ana: someone had pushed a commit setting nvidia.com/gpu: 2 earlier — reconciler immediately reapplied it -> pods get scheduled, evicted, rescheduled repeatedly.
ops-sre: plan: 1) open an emergency PR with the lower GPU values + temporary annotation `redwood/rollout-paused: "true"` so the GitOps operator preserves the emergency change 2) request quota increase + evaluate switching some requests to on-demand (non-spot) pool 3) consider pausing canary automation if it keeps bouncing traffic.
liam: FYI terraform state shows autoscaler min/max drift — someone manually increased nodepool max to absorb failed pods and GitOps is trying to revert that. that explains reconcile pressure.
maria: cost-wise this is bad: failed allocs + churned pods burned ~14 GPU-hours in the last 2 hours. spike visible on the infra-cost dashboard. we should throttle non-critical batch while we stabilize.
ana: opening PR now and tagging infra-approvers. @ops-sre can you file the quota request? also can we add an immediate route fallback to the CPU-only variant for low-priority /embed requests?
ops-sre: ticket created (#4528). I've applied a temporary taint on GPU nodes to prevent non-critical batch from grabbing GPUs during the cutover. Also adding a route policy to shove background traffic to cpu-variant until quota clears.
liam: watchout: pausing canary helps short-term but hides the reconcile-induced instability — we should add a guard in progressive-delivery to detect frequent reconcile flips and extend the stability window instead of flipping traffic quickly. filing a follow-up ticket.
maria: PR merged. GitOps reclamation should propagate in ~40s. once reconciler settles, we can unpause canary and ramp slowly. please monitor cluster Autoscaler events and the GPU allocation metric.
ana: new pods are scheduling on nodes with the temp taint and coming up Ready. traffic now at 12%.
liam: marking for postmortem. root cause = regional GPU quota exhaustion + GitOps/terraform reconcile flip + aggressive canary thresholds that reacted to transient allocation failures. mitigation: emergency repo patch, temporary taints, quota request, route-level fallback, and add reconcile-awareness to canary automation.
ops-sre: ETA on quota uplift unknown. leaving the taint in place for another 2 hours.
maria: noted — will slack finance for the cost spike. add cost tags to the emergency commit so we can attribute GPU-hours to this event.
nana: thanks all, updating ticket and the incident board. will close thread when traffic fully back to target and autoscaler is stable.
